A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MagicPose4D. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison; extraction gaps were resolved through visual inspection.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on DAVIS and PlanetZoo, motion-transfer results, and user studies in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: v2 retains original reconstruction and motion-transfer results and adds generation comparisons, a 30-prompt user-study table, and template-free skeleton examples.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain the dual-phase reconstruction, optional-template skeletonization, extendable bones, global-local Chamfer loss, and motion-transfer procedure. Newly named image-to-3D models and evaluation configurations do not establish a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: DAVIS, PlanetZoo, DeformingThings4D, and EverybodyDanceNow remain covered. v2 broadens the tested target-object categories through Figure 4 and Table 5, including jelly man, Venom, unicorn, rhino, and triceratops examples, while retaining the same reconstruction, generation, and motion-transfer tasks.

E2.justification: v2 adds LIMR and S3O to the reconstruction comparison in Table 2. Generation comparisons expand beyond Animate124 to 4Dfy, DMT+Stag4D, and SVD+Stag4D in Table 1, with DG4D and Stag4D also displayed in Figure 8. The original motion-transfer comparators remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds a 30-prompt generation evaluation addressing appearance, motion-description agreement, and overall quality, plus SVD/DMT-to-Stag4D comparison procedures. Appendix A.5 additionally describes a three-object, three-view study. These substantially extend the evaluation design, although the new studies' scales and correspondence to reported tables are incompletely reconciled.

E4.justification: v2 adds a qualitative examination of template-free skeleton extraction for wolf and bear, showing two poses from two views in Figure 10. The local-Chamfer, temporal-consistency, and self-occlusion diagnostics are retained from v1 Figure 7 as v2 Figure 6.

E5.justification: v1 reports multiple runs without specifying their number, and its table caption singles out several classes. v2 explicitly reports five runs for all compared methods and broadens the caption's averaging statement. This clarifies run counts and reporting scope without establishing an increase in runs; neither version reports dispersion or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: MagicPose4D's reported average keypoint accuracy changes from 72.4 in v1 Table 1 to 74.2 in v2 Table 2, alongside new LIMR and S3O results. v2 also adds extensive generation ratings and visual results. Matching reconstruction configurations across versions are not established. The original motion-transfer and Animate124 user-study scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The representation definitions, skeletal assumptions, blend-skinning equation, Chamfer objectives, and appendix loss equations retain their mathematical substance. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The principal contributions remain controllable 4D generation, dual-phase reconstruction, global-local Chamfer loss, and temporally consistent cross-category motion transfer. Mesh-sequence prompts become explicit in v2's abstract but were already included in v1's introduction and method.

C2.justification: New Appendix A.1 explains how correct surface reconstruction can coexist with implausible rigging and why directly transferring SE(3) transformations across different body proportions is unsuitable. Section 4.3 also explains the emphasis on keypoint accuracy for motion extraction. The principal limitations and broader-impact discussion remain.

D1.justification: v2 identifies Zero123 and SF3D as image-to-3D components and explicitly documents template-free reconstruction evaluation following S3O. Reported reconstruction time changes from 10 to 5 hours on an L40S, while listed training hyperparameters remain unchanged. Project and supplementary-video links are updated, and v1's detailed video index is removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and discussion concerning S3O, SF3D, DMT, and Stag4D, and categorizes generation methods by motion-control inputs. The main related-work narrative remains substantially unchanged. Publication updates for already cited works such as LIMR and 4Dfy do not constitute new research coverage.

P1.justification: The experiments are reordered to lead with generation and divided into task-specific subsections. v2 adds a reconstruction-explanation appendix and acknowledgments, expands captions, and edits the abstract and author block. Much of the introduction, related work, method, and conclusion remains closely matched.

P2.justification: v2 substantially revises Figures 4 and 8, adds the skeleton illustration and generation-study tables, and removes the video-index table. The reconstruction comparison and original Animate124 study move into the appendix. Changed typography, caption lengths, table structures, and figure placement broadly revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 adds more relevant motion-control baselines and clearer methodological explanations. However, its central new Table 1 reports ratings up to 5.39, while Appendix A.5 explicitly documents only 0–5 scales and inconsistently describes the linked study's methods and criteria. The new study's scale and protocol remain unresolved, preventing a reliable assessment of the net benefit of the expanded evidence.
